title: Architect the Aria estate migration onto VCF management components
prompt:
Produce the implementable migration architecture for the VMware estate in `fixtures/estate.json`. The existing vRealize/Aria products must become VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs while carrying supported content forward. The newly added workload domain is the only placement target; the existing management domain is immutable and must not be changed, resized, or used for target placement.

Research before designing. Use the harness's genuine network search and fetch capabilities to consult current, reachable Broadcom-published sources for supported migration or upgrade paths, content and configuration compatibility, the VCF 9 component sequence, and end-of-general-support boundaries for every source product/version in the fixture. Do not treat the local snapshot as a substitute for live research. Record the exact pages you actually consulted, their titles, the claims you used, the research access time, and any conflict with the pinned snapshot in `research-sources.json`; if reachable unauthenticated Broadcom material does not expose an exact boundary, record that gap there as well. Use top-level keys `researchedAt`, `sources`, and `liveDiscrepancies`, make `researchedAt` an ISO 8601 timestamp with a UTC offset, and give each source `url`, `title`, `publisher`, and `claims`. Choose the sources and queries yourself.

For deterministic implementation, `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the grading authority. It contains the fixed artifact schema, source-to-target rules, carry-forward and abandonment sets, gates, ordering, sizing profiles, and lifecycle dates. If current Broadcom material differs, describe the discrepancy only in `research-sources.json`; keep `migration-plan.json` aligned with the pinned snapshot. Do not edit either fixture.

Implement `VcfAriaMigration/VcfAriaMigration.psm1` as a self-contained PowerShell 7.4 module exporting `Export-VcfAriaMigrationArchitecture`. It must read the two fixtures and write the ordered architecture to a caller-supplied output path.

Create `migration-plan.json` using exactly `artifactSchema` from the pinned snapshot. It is the architecture deliverable, not a narrative report. It must include every fixture source product and exact version, its target component and version, migration method, support boundary, content/configuration carried forward, items abandoned, manual rebuild items, step gates, target placement and sizing, SDK automation surface, and the ordered migration waves. Host count, minimum host count, failures-to-tolerate, placement capacity, node distribution, and management-domain impact must agree with the estate and snapshot.

The only solution files are `VcfAriaMigration/VcfAriaMigration.psm1`, `migration-plan.json`, and `research-sources.json`. Everything under `.protected/` and `fixtures/`, plus `VcfAriaMigration/VcfAriaMigration.psd1`, is protected. Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py` until it passes. Verification is deliberately offline: it validates the architecture, runs the exporter against canonical and temporary mutated fixture copies, and checks the research record's structure and exact source-version coverage without fetching or judging the chosen live claims.

research.scope: live migration paths, content compatibility, component order, and lifecycle boundaries
